92030→##### D.110c-0a bounded epoch-relative seal-custody plan

The completed source audit pins the exact defect and prevents a broader seal
redesign. `packages/protocol-v3/src/seal.ts` holds `SealAuthorityState.epoch` as
literal `0`, rejects genuine creator trust when `material.currentEpoch !== 0`,
and registers every authority identity at epoch 0. `packages/seal` repeats that
literal in voter enrollment, vote/round-change intent, pacemaker event, and
creator-close evidence types. The browser `voteSlots`, `signerState`,
`voteOutbox`, and `sealEvidence` schemas already key by epoch under schema v3,
but their adapters validate, read, and write only epoch 0. Finally,
92040→`openBrowserSealEvidenceStore().servePeerEvidence({objectId, signerId})`
hardcodes `[objectId, 0, signerId]`, while the Node recovery request already
carries the authority's authenticated epoch. The actor additionally calls an
unscoped evidence `readAll()` and enforces `rows.length <= 1` across the whole
database, so a retained epoch-0 record can block or be resumed by an epoch-1
actor even after the literal authority guard is removed. The vote dispatcher
also encodes `row.epoch` but marks `[objectId, 0, ...]` dispatched. The
production seam is therefore composition, exact-row selection, and literal
narrowing across existing owners; no wire record, cryptographic rule, or
database schema change is indicated.
92050→
D.110c-0a is one security-authority TDD slice with two diagnostic batches and
one final GREEN review. Its owner paths are:

- `packages/protocol-v3/src/seal.ts` and private seal-authority identity/custody;
- `packages/seal/src/creator.ts`, `pacemaker.ts`, and private creator-close,
  vote-intent, evidence-enumeration, and storage-port custody;
- `packages/node/src/creator-seal.ts` and only the actor-opening binding in
  `packages/node/src/creator-close.ts`, without changing network request bytes
  or the exported close result;
92060→- `packages/storage-browser/src/seal-vote.ts`, `seal-evidence.ts`, and the
  internal vote/evidence adapters, including `seal-vote-dispatch.ts`;
- `packages/storage-browser/src/internal/seal-vote-test-control.ts` only as a
  deterministic tests-only carrier/helper owner; it does not define product
  authority or acceptance; and
- schema-v3 only as a source-shape invariant: its existing epoch-bearing keys
  remain byte-for-byte and no version bump is expected.

The public compatibility decision is exact. The evidence-serving selector
becomes the closed union
92070→`{objectId, signerId} | {objectId, epoch, signerId}`. The legacy two-field form
means epoch 0 only; it never means latest, maximum, active, or any other stored
epoch. The three-field form requires a nonnegative safe-integer epoch and reads
the exact `[objectId, epoch, signerId]` row. Extra keys, malformed epoch, and
cross-object/signer inputs fail before I/O under the existing public
`TypeError("peer evidence identity is invalid")` owner. The internal evidence
adapter always requires explicit epoch. This selector union is the only planned
new public input shape in 0a. The exported fields that widen from literal `0`
to a nonnegative safe integer are exactly `SealAuthorityState.epoch`,
`SealAuthorityIdentity.epoch`, `SealVoterEnrollmentData.epoch`,
92080→`CreatorCloseEvidenceRecord.epoch`, `PacemakerEvent.epoch`, and the browser
`PendingVoteRow.epoch` plus `InternalSealVoteStore.markDispatched` tuple epoch.
`CreatorLiveCloseResult.epoch` and
`CreatorLiveCloseResult.successorEpoch`, including the literal values returned
by `bindCreatorLiveClose`, remain owned by D.110c-a and are explicitly out of
0a. Every epoch-0 value and byte remains unchanged. If implementation requires
another public API, a schema version, wire field, dependency, or migration
carrier, stop and reslice.

RED batch 1 uses the genuine adopted epoch-1 creator trust already produced by
92090→the retained D.108 path. It attempts to open the real creator seal authority
and freezes today's causal failure without fixture-authored QC/trust bytes:

- genuine epoch-1 `openSealAuthority` returns exact `untrusted-context` solely
  because of the `currentEpoch !== 0` guard; the evidence must pair the same
  genuine signer and epoch-0 trust success with the genuine successor-trust
  failure plus the exact source predicate, because the error string alone also
  owns foreign-trust rejection;
- tests-only compile/source-shape assertions separately enumerate the existing
  seal/intent/pacemaker/evidence literal narrowings; they do not bypass the
92100→  refusal or produce bytes admissible as GREEN evidence; and
- certified/BFT trust remains epoch-0-only and is not generalized by this
  creator slice.

RED batch 2 must remain executable before GREEN, so it does not claim that
today's product minted an epoch-1 authority, vote, or QC. It uses exact
tests-only canonical carrier bytes signed by the genuine D.108 creator key to
diagnose the adapter/key/selector epoch-0 narrowing; those carriers and any raw
IndexedDB insertion are labelled negative discriminators and are never
admissible as production authority or GREEN success evidence. It proves the
92110→schema can distinguish epoch-0 and epoch-1 rows for the same object/signer but
the adapters cannot select/write/read the epoch-1 discriminator and the public
two-field evidence selector can only return epoch 0. GREEN batch 2 must then
rederive the successful epoch-1 rows through the genuine actor path. Each RED
batch runs its focused non-campaign test exactly once before any production
edit. Any failure outside the frozen matrix stops diagnosis before more
changes. The diagnostic encoder uses only the existing registry-v1 `sealVote`,
`sealQC`, and cut kinds/domains and records its exact bytes and digests; it does
not invent a fixture-only wire kind.

92120→GREEN batch 1 generalizes only opaque authenticated custody:

- `SealAuthorityState.epoch`, authority identity, voter enrollment, intent,
  pacemaker events, creator evidence, and pending rows carry a copied
  nonnegative safe-integer epoch derived from genuine trust/authority;
- the creator branch of `openSealAuthority` accepts every genuine current
  creator epoch, binds the current anchor/object/signer set, and registers that
  exact epoch; the certified/BFT branch retains its exact epoch-0 contract;
- no caller-supplied epoch can mint or retarget authority, and forged structural
  trust/authority/enrollment/intent objects remain `untrusted-context` or their
92130→  existing exact untrusted-capability error;
- vote, proposal, round-change, prepare-QC, commit-QC, cut, and successor-trust
  verification all compare exact object/epoch/anchor/value/round/signer facts;
  cross-epoch replay retains the existing exact `cut-binding-mismatch`,
  `qc-binding-mismatch`, `round-change-binding-mismatch`,
  `proposal-binding-mismatch`, or `leader-vote-binding-mismatch` owner; and
- epoch-0 vectors and canonical registered bytes remain byte-identical.

GREEN batch 2 generalizes the mechanical browser owners:

92140→- every vote/evidence state key, slot, outbox row, snapshot scope, pending row,
  dispatched key, and peer-evidence lookup uses the authenticated explicit
  epoch rather than literal 0;
- the vote row-key epoch is derived from decoded authenticated vote/QC bytes or
  the resolved opaque round-change intent, and every redundant mechanical input
  epoch must equal it; a key/input epoch that differs from the authenticated
  carrier fails with exact `MALFORMED_INPUT` before a write;
- the four stores isolate revision, lock, prepare/commit QC, equivocation,
  pending dispatch, and evidence state by exact `(objectId, epoch, signerId)`;
  activity in epoch N cannot occupy, advance, dispatch, overwrite, or satisfy
92150→  epoch N+1;
- the public evidence-selector union preserves legacy epoch-0 behavior and
  returns only the explicitly selected epoch for the new form. Rejecting extra
  selector keys tightens today's destructuring behavior; the responder is
  currently wired only by retained Phase-5e test assets, while the production
  Node request already carries authenticated epoch, so this declared tightening
  has no hidden production caller;
- schema authority remains version 3 with unchanged key paths, so no IndexedDB
  migration is manufactured; existing epoch-0 rows reopen unchanged; and
- creator evidence open/resume selects only the exact current-trust
92160→  `(objectId, epoch, anchor, signerId)` record before enforcing the one-record

92045	actor even after the literal authority guard is removed. The vote dispatcher
92046	also encodes `row.epoch` but marks `[objectId, 0, ...]` dispatched. The
92047	production seam is therefore composition, exact-row selection, and literal
92048	narrowing across existing owners; no wire record, cryptographic rule, or
92049	database schema change is indicated.
92050	
92051	D.110c-0a is one security-authority TDD slice with two diagnostic batches and
92052	one final GREEN review. Its owner paths are:
92053	
92054	- `packages/protocol-v3/src/seal.ts` and private seal-authority identity/custody;

92069	becomes the closed union
92070	`{objectId, signerId} | {objectId, epoch, signerId}`. The legacy two-field form
92071	means epoch 0 only; it never means latest, maximum, active, or any other stored
92072	epoch. The three-field form requires a nonnegative safe-integer epoch and reads
92073	the exact `[objectId, epoch, signerId]` row. Extra keys, malformed epoch, and
92074	cross-object/signer inputs fail before I/O under the existing public
92075	`TypeError("peer evidence identity is invalid")` owner. The internal evidence
92076	adapter always requires explicit epoch. This selector union is the only planned
92077	new public input shape in 0a. The exported fields that widen from literal `0`

92079	`SealAuthorityIdentity.epoch`, `SealVoterEnrollmentData.epoch`,

92031	
92032	The completed source audit pins the exact defect and prevents a broader seal
92033	redesign. `packages/protocol-v3/src/seal.ts` holds `SealAuthorityState.epoch` as
92034	literal `0`, rejects genuine creator trust when `material.currentEpoch !== 0`,
92035	and registers every authority identity at epoch 0. `packages/seal` repeats that
92036	literal in voter enrollment, vote/round-change intent, pacemaker event, and
92037	creator-close evidence types. The browser `voteSlots`, `signerState`,
92038	`voteOutbox`, and `sealEvidence` schemas already key by epoch under schema v3,
92039	but their adapters validate, read, and write only epoch 0. Finally,
92040	`openBrowserSealEvidenceStore().servePeerEvidence({objectId, signerId})`
92041	hardcodes `[objectId, 0, signerId]`, while the Node recovery request already
92042	carries the authority's authenticated epoch. The actor additionally calls an
92043	unscoped evidence `readAll()` and enforces `rows.length <= 1` across the whole
92044	database, so a retained epoch-0 record can block or be resumed by an epoch-1
92045	actor even after the literal authority guard is removed. The vote dispatcher
92046	also encodes `row.epoch` but marks `[objectId, 0, ...]` dispatched. The
92047	production seam is therefore composition, exact-row selection, and literal
92048	narrowing across existing owners; no wire record, cryptographic rule, or
92049	database schema change is indicated.
92050	
92051	D.110c-0a is one security-authority TDD slice with two diagnostic batches and
92052	one final GREEN review. Its owner paths are:
92053	
92054	- `packages/protocol-v3/src/seal.ts` and private seal-authority identity/custody;
92055	- `packages/seal/src/creator.ts`, `pacemaker.ts`, and private creator-close,

92071	means epoch 0 only; it never means latest, maximum, active, or any other stored
92072	epoch. The three-field form requires a nonnegative safe-integer epoch and reads
